subject.title: Discord compaction still fails with provider_error_4xx after #90496 closure on 2026.6.5

question: When Codex native compaction returns provider_error_4xx for a Discord channel session, should OpenClaw rotate/preserve the transcript into a fresh usable session, surface an actionable recovery path without rotation, or treat the 4xx as an external auth/config failure?
rationale: The source and issue logs show the failure boundary, but choosing automatic rotation versus actionable fail-closed recovery changes session-state and Discord user experience semantics.

options.title: Define Recovery Policy First
options.body: Run or request a live Discord/Codex repro, then implement the selected provider-4xx recovery behavior with focused session and Codex bridge coverage.

options.title: Treat As External Auth Failure
options.body: Keep fail-closed behavior but make the Discord reply and diagnostics explicitly explain the Codex 403 cause and supported recovery steps.

options.title: Fold Into Timeout Work Only
options.body: Close this only if the timeout-progress fix is proven with live Discord/Codex provider-4xx evidence, otherwise it leaves the reported 403 path unowned.

recommendation.title: Define Recovery Policy First
recommendation.body: Run or request a live Discord/Codex repro, then implement the selected provider-4xx recovery behavior with focused session and Codex bridge coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent adjacent Codex app-server/harness ownership history and is the strongest maintainer-routing candidate among the inspected owners for a product/session policy choice.
